title: Four 12.5 Mb runs of N may sort 40 times slower without the N-run shortcut
body:
Since 665ee89 on `dev`, `find_lcp` in `libsufr/src/sufr_builder.rs` has no special case for runs of `N`. Comparisons between suffixes inside long runs rely on the skip in the LCP-aware merge and on `LcpCache` in `libsufr/src/lcp.rs`. `LcpCache` stores LCPs of 1,024 or more, keyed by the distance between the two suffixes, and `lcp_avx2` probes it every 1,024 scanned bytes.

One synthetic input took 40 times longer without the shortcut. It was 100 Mb of random ACGT with four runs of 12.5 Mb of `N`, built with `create -t 4 -n 256 -d -a`.

| input | with the shortcut | without |
|---|---|---|
| four runs of 12.5 Mb | about 9.5 s | 415 s, one run |
| one run of 50 Mb | 8.2-8.3 s | 10.4-11.0 s |

The 415 s run was never repeated, and it was being stopped as it finished. hg38 does not show the problem: it has 488 runs, and at 32 threads it builds in 121-136 s without the shortcut.

## Open

- Whether the 415 s repeats. Rebuild the input and time 665ee89 on it.
- If it does, why the cache misses. Two untested guesses: the first comparison between two different runs is at a distance not yet in the cache, and each rayon worker has its own `LcpCache`, so an entry one worker stores is not seen by another.
close_reason: Dropped: inputs made mostly of a few multi-Mb runs of N are too unlikely in practice to justify checking the 415 s case.
